meta.disclaimer: Rental terms, cross-border fees, and waiver options vary by company and vehicle class. Confirm in writing before collection — Savanna Explorer does not book rentals.
meta.sourceLabel: National tourism boards & AA South Africa cross-border guidance

intro: Most self-drive safaris start with a South African or Namibian rental. This guide covers vehicle choice, cross-border paperwork, gravel damage waivers, and the kit list operators expect you to carry.

vehicleTypes.bestFor: Tarred highways, city gateways, Eswatini, Lesotho lowlands (not Sani Pass)
vehicleTypes.avoid: Deep sand (Chobe, Kalahari), Sani Pass, remote Damaraland tracks, Ponta sand track
vehicleTypes.notes: Lower fuel use and easier parking in towns. Most Kruger public roads are tar — 4×2 is fine inside the park.

vehicleTypes.bestFor: Namibia gravel, Botswana sand edges, Sani Pass, Moremi public camps, overland loops
vehicleTypes.avoid: Assuming AWD equals ground clearance — check wading depth and tyre size
vehicleTypes.notes: Request high clearance, diesel for range, and two spare tyres in Namibia. Manual common — specify automatic if needed.

vehicleTypes.bestFor: Namibia self-drive camping, remote Botswana, multi-week loops
vehicleTypes.avoid: Short city breaks — excess equipment and higher daily rate
vehicleTypes.notes: Includes rooftop tent, fridge, chairs, often second spare. One-way fees between Windhoek and Cape Town common.

crossBorderLetter.title: Cross-border letter of authority
crossBorderLetter.body: Financed and rental vehicles need written permission naming every country, dates, drivers, registration, and VIN. Border officials match this to your passport and windshield disc.
bullets: Request 5–7 days before pickup — not at the counter on collection day
Typical rental fee: ZAR 1,000–1,500 per border crossing (paid to the company, not at the post)
List every country you might enter — ad-hoc additions are rarely approved at the border
Owned outright: original registration in your name + insurance; financed cars still need bank consent
Lesotho and Eswatini must be named explicitly on SA rentals — do not assume they are included

gravelWaiver.title: Gravel road & tyre damage waivers
gravelWaiver.body: Standard collision damage waiver often excludes windscreen chips, tyre punctures, and undercarriage damage on gravel — where most Namibia and Botswana incidents happen.
bullets: Buy super cover or gravel waiver where offered (often ZAR/NAD 100–200/day extra)
Two spare tyres mandatory for remote Namibia — some companies include, others charge deposit
Return vehicle with same tyre count; puncture repair receipts help dispute claims
Sand driving (Chobe, Kalahari) may void cover without 4×4 experience — read the fine print

kitList: Two reflective triangles + fire extinguisher (SA cross-border requirement)
Warning triangle and hi-vis vest per passenger in some countries
Tyre pressure gauge and compressor (Namibia gravel)
Jumper cables or portable jump pack
Tow rope rated for vehicle weight
Offline maps downloaded (Maps.me, Google offline, or GPS unit)
ZAR/USD cash in small notes for tolls and border desks
Physical copy of cross-border letter and Yellow Card
Phone mount and car charger — handheld phone use illegal in SA
Cooler box and drinking water for desert legs
Basic tool kit and duct tape for gravel track repairs

countries.title: South Africa — rental hub
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 for tar circuits; 4×4 only for Sani Pass, Richtersveld, deep sand
countries.crossBorder: Avis, Europcar, Tempest, Bidvest — all offer cross-border letters for a fee
countries.planningTip: SANRAL e-tag for Gauteng tolls; request Lesotho/Eswatini on the letter for Kingdom Circuit loops.

countries.title: Namibia — 4×4 self-drive
countries.pickupHubs: Windhoek (WDH), Walvis Bay, one-way to CPT possible
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×4 with two spares standard for gravel; sedan only for tar-only routes
countries.crossBorder: Namibia2Go, Asco, Thrifty — confirm Botswana/Zambia letters if looping
countries.planningTip: Book compressor and rooftop tent early in peak season (Jun–Oct).

countries.title: Botswana — Maun & Kasane
countries.pickupHubs: Maun (MUB), Kasane; limited fleet vs SA
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×4 for Moremi, Chobe sand, and Kalahari tracks
countries.crossBorder: Fewer cross-border options — many fly to Maun and rent locally
countries.planningTip: Most Delta camps are fly-in; self-drive suits Chobe and Moremi public camps.

countries.title: Zambia — Livingstone & Lusaka
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 OK for Livingstone–Chobe day trips with guide; 4×4 for Liuwa and remote parks
countries.crossBorder: Limited international one-way — often SA rental with letter into Zambia
countries.planningTip: Proflight often faster than driving Lusaka–Mfuwe on the Great North Road.

countries.title: Zimbabwe — Victoria Falls & Harare
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 for Vic Falls–Hwange tar; 4×4 for Gonarezhou and remote tracks
countries.crossBorder: SA rental with letter common for KAZA loops; local hire for in-country only
countries.planningTip: Fuel shortages possible — fill in Vic Falls or Harare before remote legs.

countries.title: Mozambique — Maputo & coast
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 for EN1 tar; 4×4 for Ponta sand track and northern sand roads
countries.crossBorder: SA rental via Lebombo common; confirm Mozambique on letter
countries.planningTip: Do not drive EN1 at night — checkpoints and livestock on road.

countries.title: Malawi — Lilongwe & Blantyre
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 for Lake Malawi shore; 4×4 for Nyika Plateau wet season
countries.crossBorder: Often entered via Zambia (Mchinji) with SA or Zambian rental letter
countries.planningTip: Fuel can be scarce — carry cash and top up in major towns.

countries.title: Lesotho — SA rental extension
countries.pickupHubs: No major international fleet — use SA rental with Lesotho on letter
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×4 mandatory for Sani Pass; tar to Maseru and Afriski in dry season
countries.crossBorder: Name Lesotho explicitly; guided Sani tours from Underberg if not confident
countries.planningTip: No fuel on Sani Pass — fill Maseru or Underberg before ascending.

countries.title: Eswatini — Kruger add-on
countries.pickupHubs: Use SA rental from JNB or MQP with Eswatini on letter
countries.vehicleAdvice: 4×2 sufficient — excellent tar on EZ1 highway
countries.crossBorder: Oshoek from Gauteng; Golela from KZN — both need letter permission
countries.planningTip: Compact country — breakfast in highveld, afternoon game drive in lowveld same day.
